data.title: AI | Oracle Results Ease Concerns Over Its AI Infrastructure Buildout
data.description:
Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow breaks down Oracle's latest results and says they are helping ease concerns about the company's massive AI infrastructure buildout, according to Bloomberg.

He also discusses the growing debate over AI's societal risks and the backlash against the global data center build-out.

data.title: GXO Logistics Sees New-Business Wins, Wincanton Synergies Driving Margin Growth
data.description: According to CNBC, GXO Logistics is seeing accelerating new-business wins that the company and analysts expect to support future revenue growth and margin expansion, while its shares have lagged peers and trade at about 8x forward enterprise value-to-Ebitda. The company said new business wins rose 34% year over year to $410 million in the second quarter, and Wincanton integration is expected to deliver $60 million in cost savings by the end of the year. GXO plans to hold an investor day on Nov. 16, where management is expected to provide more detail on growth, margins and capital deployment. The company also said it will continue buying back shares in the back half of the year.

data.title: Johnson & Johnson Bets On Ottava To Challenge Intuitive Surgical In Robotic Surgery
data.description:
According to CNBC, Johnson & Johnson is pushing into the robotic surgery market with Ottava, which received Food and Drug Administration approval this summer for use in multiple general surgery procedures. The company said the system’s smaller footprint and design features could help it win over surgeons and hospitals, while its surgery business generated $5.16 billion in revenue in the first six months of the year, up 4.3% from a year earlier.

Hani Abouhalka, head of J&J’s surgery and robotics unit, said the company aims to become a leader in surgical robotics. Precedence Research projects the U.S. surgical robotics market will grow from about $4.4 billion in 2025 to $18.75 billion by 2035, while the global market is expected to rise from $14.45 billion in 2026 to about $50.29 billion by 2035. Ottava is approved for 10 general surgery procedures, and J&J said it is pursuing additional approvals in Western Europe and Japan as part of its rollout.

data.title: Mitsubishi UFJ Expects a 25-Basis-Point Fed Hike This Month, Then No Change in October
data.description:
Mitsubishi UFJ has dropped its forecast that the Federal Reserve would keep rates unchanged this year and now expects the central bank to raise rates by 25 basis points in September. According to Sina Finance, strategists George Goncalves and Agron Nicaj cited Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish remarks at Jackson Hole, solid August employment data, and Friday's hotter-than-expected CPI.

The strategists wrote that a rate hike could amount to a "policy mistake," but said the Fed would find it difficult to stand pat when markets already expect a hike next week. They also said that if Warsh repeatedly stresses that "inflation is one of the options" and does nothing, it would create problems.

Mitsubishi UFJ expects the Fed to leave rates unchanged in October after the September hike, saying officials are unlikely to signal an aggressive push into the tightening cycle before the midterm elections. The strategists put the probability of another rate hike in December at 55% to 60%.

They also raised their yield forecasts for most maturities of U.S. Treasuries by 25 to 50 basis points. They now expect year-end yields of 4.25% for the two-year Treasury, 4.625% for the 10-year, and 5% for the 30-year.

The strategists still said U.S. Treasuries could have room to rise if economic growth weakens in 2027, inflation cools, or fiscal consolidation expectations increase.

data.title: Arizona, Pennsylvania Election Officials Ban Workers From Prediction Market Contracts
data.description: According to CNBC, election and county officials in Arizona and Pennsylvania are barring employees from participating in prediction market contracts tied to elections, citing concerns that workers with access to ballots could use non-public information. Maricopa County supervisor Thomas Galvin said the county adopted a July resolution covering about 13,000 employees and that Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs signed an executive order banning state workers from insider trading on prediction markets. Delaware County, Pennsylvania, also banned roughly 2,200 employees from trading on election-linked prediction market contracts, while Maryland's elections administrator asked the state prosecutor in July to investigate whether such contracts violate state law. Officials said prediction market odds can be confused with polling, and Kalshi and Polymarket said they have taken steps to prevent insider trading on their platforms.
